description: Downtown Portland's Vinyl Headquarters since 1982Established in 1982, 2ND AVENUE RECORDS is a quintessential brick and mortar independent record store.  Our store is centrally located in downtown near the historic Saturday Market, Voodoo Doughnut, and Kells Irish Pub.
review_summary:
According to its own official website, 2nd Avenue Records is one of Portland's most enduring independent record stores, having operated continuously since 1982 in the heart of downtown near landmarks like Voodoo Doughnut and the historic Saturday Market. The shop carries a wide-ranging inventory of new and used vinyl, CDs, and cassettes spanning rock, jazz, soul, funk, rap, blues, reggae, metal, punk, and 1960s classics, and is also noted for a large t-shirt selection — a hallmark of the classic American indie record store experience. Having expanded from a 600 sq ft original storefront to its current location at 121 SW 2nd Avenue, the shop has demonstrated staying power in a challenging retail environment.

However, a comprehensive third-party review analysis is significantly hampered by the near-total absence of usable independent customer reviews in available sources. The loc8nearme.com listing returned only an unrendered JavaScript template with no actual ratings or review content, and no Yelp, Google, Discogs, or social media review data was surfaced. This gap makes it impossible to independently verify the quality of the in-store experience, staff expertise, pricing competitiveness, or inventory condition from a customer perspective. The shop's own website also shows signs of neglect, with both the 'About' and 'About Us' pages returning 404 errors.

For anyone visiting Portland's downtown core, 2nd Avenue Records represents a genuine piece of the city's independent music retail history and is worth a visit for dedicated crate-diggers and casual browsers alike. That said, prospective visitors should note the limited hours (noon to 5 pm daily) and should verify current operating status before making a trip, given the incomplete state of the shop's online presence. The shop accepts walk-in collection purchases without an appointment, which is a notable and practical perk for sellers.

long_description: Rock of Ages Music Art & Memorabilia has earned a reputation as one of Nashville's coolest destinations for music lovers, offering an eclectic mix of vinyl record art and music memorabilia that spans genres and generations. The shop specializes in uniquely crafted vinyl record artwork — pieces that transform classic albums into striking visual art — featuring an impressive roster of artists ranging from country legends like George Jones, Keith Whitley, and Kenny Chesney to rock icons like Black Sabbath, Kurt Cobain, and the Beatles, alongside contemporary acts like Chappell Roan and Billy Strings. With over 230 pieces available, the collection is a testament to the store's broad musical passion and its commitment to celebrating music culture in a city that lives and breathes it. The shop carries an unmistakable energy that resonates with both die-hard collectors and casual visitors looking for something genuinely memorable to take home from Nashville. Operating both as a brick-and-mortar destination and an online shop with free shipping on record art, Rock of Ages bridges the local experience with a wider audience, making its one-of-a-kind offerings accessible to music fans well beyond Music City's borders.

long_description: Dead End Records is a Nashville, Tennessee record shop with an unapologetically cool, no-frills personality — they'll be the first to tell you they're better experienced in person. Open every day except Tuesday, the shop specializes in vinyl records, cassette tapes, and CDs spanning a distinctly heavy and alternative edge, with inventory ranging from doom and metal acts like Monolord, Elvenking, and Mefisto to post-hardcore staples like Fugazi and Title Fight. What truly sets Dead End Records apart is its deep commitment to the local music scene, offering a playful "Blind Date with a Local Band" feature that lets customers discover Nashville artists through mystery purchases — a charming way to champion homegrown talent. Beyond music, the shop carries band merch, patches and pins, mugs, stained glass, and apparel, making it a destination for the broader underground music community. Pre-orders for upcoming releases keep dedicated collectors in the loop, while used vinyl rounds out the selection for diggers on a budget. Irreverent, community-rooted, and genre-savvy, Dead End Records carves out its own lane in a city better known for country music.

long_description: Tucked along Lebanon Pike in the Donelson neighborhood of Nashville, Tennessee, Analog Your Life is a vinyl-focused record shop that invites music lovers to slow down and reconnect with the tactile pleasure of physical music. Open seven days a week from 11 AM to 6 PM, the shop maintains an accessible, laid-back schedule that welcomes both serious collectors and casual browsers alike. Specializing in vinyl records, the store curates a full inventory that spans genres and eras, catering to the diverse tastes of Nashville's passionate music community. What sets Analog Your Life apart is its commitment to meeting collectors where they are — whether that means browsing the shelves in person or shopping remotely through their active Discogs page, which extends their reach well beyond Middle Tennessee. The shop carries a spirit that feels deeply personal, with direct owner contact through email and phone reflecting a hands-on, community-minded approach to running an independent record store. In a city built on musical heritage, Analog Your Life offers a warm, unhurried destination for anyone who still believes the best way to experience music is needle to groove.

description: We’re throwin’ the doors wide and crankin’ up the volume—ETRS is officially open, with four floors of live music, cold drinks, a rooftop bar overlooking Broadway, and a shop full of vinyl.  It’s all about the records, live music, and the Nashville roots that make this landmark sing—just like it always has.
long_description: Since 1947, the Ernest Tubb Record Shop has been one of Nashville's most storied landmarks, rooted in a deep love for country music and the vinyl records that carry its legacy. Founded by the Texas Troubadour himself, the Broadway institution spent decades welcoming music fans and rising talents by day while hosting the legendary Midnite Jamboree by night — a stage that drew icons like Loretta Lynn, Hank Williams, Dolly Parton, and Johnny Cash. Today, the reimagined ETRS has expanded into a sprawling five-floor experience that balances its record shop roots with live music venues, hidden lounges, cold drinks, and a rooftop bar with sweeping views of Broadway. The vinyl remains central to the whole operation, grounding everything in the Nashville tradition that made this place matter in the first place. Whether you're flipping through records or catching a live set on one of the upper floors, the energy here feels earned — layered with decades of real country music history and a genuine commitment to keeping that spirit alive and loud for generations to come.

long_description: Third Man Records is a Nashville, Tennessee institution that functions as far more than a traditional record shop — it's a fully realized music ecosystem built around a deep, almost obsessive love of vinyl and live sound. Founded by Jack White, the label and storefront specializes in vinyl releases spanning indie rock, blues, folk, and experimental music, with a catalog that ranges from White's own projects to carefully curated archival releases and newly discovered recordings like those of the late Connie Converse. The Nashville location houses The Blue Room, an intimate venue that hosts a steady stream of live performances and direct-to-acetate recording sessions, giving the space a rare energy that blurs the line between record store and cultural hub. Third Man also operates a Detroit outpost in the Cass Corridor neighborhood, extending its reach beyond Tennessee. What truly sets Third Man apart is its commitment to the tactile and the analog — from its long-running Vault subscription series delivering exclusive pressings to members, to its Third Man Hardware line of guitar pedals and a collaboration with Victrola on limited-edition turntables and speakers. It is, in every sense, a place where the record is still treated as something sacred.

description: WELCOME TO VINYL TAP!
long_description: Vinyl Tap is a beloved Nashville record shop and bar born from the lifelong dream of Todd Hedrick, a ninth-generation Nashvillian who spent his youth haunting local shops like Tower Records and the Great Escape before years in corporate America finally gave way to something better. Opening its doors in November 2016, the shop is housed in a restored East Nashville building that has lived many lives — from neighborhood grocery to laundromat — and now serves as a warm gathering place for music lovers and locals alike. Vinyl Tap specializes in both new and used vinyl, carrying this week's new releases alongside an ever-growing selection of reissues, and offers a full bar featuring specialty cocktails alongside local and regional craft beers on draft, in bottles, and in cans. But what truly sets Vinyl Tap apart is its soul — it's as much a community hub as a record store, hosting weekly events like staff-curated listening nights, beginner DJ workshops, literary readings, and album release parties. With a rewards program for regulars, its own merch, and a webstore for buying and pre-ordering records, Vinyl Tap has grown into exactly the kind of neighborhood institution Nashville deserves.

long_description: Swaggie Records Nashville is a beloved independent record shop serving music lovers across Music City with two convenient locations — the original downtown store at 211 Union Street, open seven days a week, and a newer second location in the Donelson neighborhood. Rather than leaning into Nashville's country music identity, Swaggie carves out its own distinct niche by specializing in jazz, reggae, and blues — three genres that speak to the deeper roots of American and Caribbean musical tradition. Browsers can dig through classic jazz from legends like Miles Davis, John Coltrane, and Chet Baker, explore the rich rhythms of reggae from Bob Marley, King Tubby, and Toots, or trace the soulful lineage of the blues from Memphis to Muscle Shoals to Dallas. The shop's curatorial approach feels intentional and passionate, guided by a genuine reverence for these genres rather than trend-chasing. Beyond vinyl, Swaggie also offers licensed apparel, adding a lifestyle dimension to the shopping experience. With its accessible hours, dual locations, and deeply focused inventory, Swaggie Records has positioned itself as a welcoming destination for serious collectors and curious newcomers alike.

long_description: McKay's Nashville is a beloved used media emporium that has been serving music lovers and pop culture enthusiasts since opening its doors in 2007. Part of a small regional chain with roots stretching back to 1974, when the original concept was born out of a vision for accessible, community-driven learning, McKay's operates on a beautifully simple premise: customers bring in their previously loved records, books, movies, video games, and more in exchange for cash or store credit, creating an ever-rotating inventory that makes every visit feel like a treasure hunt. The record selection — spanning genres, eras, and formats — sits alongside an enormous range of other secondhand goods, meaning vinyl diggers often find themselves happily lost among collectibles, musical instruments, and vintage electronics as well. Because everything on the shelves was sourced directly from fellow Nashville residents, the stock is genuinely unpredictable, reflecting the eclectic tastes of the city itself. Open most days from morning into the evening, McKay's has cultivated a reputation as the kind of place where you come in looking for one thing and leave with five others you never knew you needed.

description: Local Record Store in Nashville, TN
long_description: Alison's Record Shop is a beloved family-owned vinyl destination tucked away in Nashville, Tennessee, offering what it proudly claims to be the greatest selection of vintage records in all of Davidson County. Specializing in LPs spanning an impressively broad range of genres — from rock and metal to 80s new wave and R&B — the shop also carries a limited selection of 45s and CDs for the dedicated collector. What truly sets Alison's apart is its commitment to quality: most records don't make it onto the shelves unless they earn a "very good" grade from the knowledgeable staff, ensuring customers take home something genuinely worth listening to. Beyond vinyl, the shop stocks premium turntables and audio equipment from respected brands like Music Hall, DALI, Magnepan, Bryston, and Marantz, making it a one-stop destination for building a serious listening setup. The atmosphere is warm and unhurried, with a laid-back environment and staff who genuinely love helping customers discover new artists and albums. Alison's also buys used records, welcoming collectors looking to pass their collections on to a good home.

long_description: Grimey's New & Preloved Music has long established itself as Nashville's premier independent record store, a beloved institution where music obsessives and casual listeners alike come to dig through an eclectic mix of new releases and preloved vinyl, CDs, and books. Located in the heart of Music City, the shop carries a palpable sense of community warmth — staff and regulars genuinely connect over shared discoveries, and the owners, Doyle and Grimey, have built something that feels more like a neighborhood gathering place than a mere retail outlet. The store's history and cultural significance were notable enough to earn a feature on PBS' Tennessee Crossroads, and in 2025 Grimey's claimed the prestigious Frontline Innovator Award at Music Biz, cementing its reputation as a forward-thinking force in independent retail. With an active web store, a Discogs presence for collectible records, and preorder options on select autographed releases, Grimey's masterfully balances old-school record shop soul with modern accessibility.

name: 939 Records
description: Pittsburgh's first online record store
review_summary:
939 Records, located in White Oak, Pennsylvania (just outside Pittsburgh), positions itself as a trailblazer in the regional vinyl market, claiming the title of 'Pittsburgh's first online record store' according to at least one visitor review. The shop operates a dedicated e-commerce storefront at 939records.com, where it lists vinyl records and CDs with clearly graded conditions using standard industry terminology (VG+, NM/M-), and offers pricing that ranges from affordable ($10 for select 12-inch singles) to collectible-tier ($40+ for rarer 10-inch pressings). The homepage inventory visible at time of analysis skews toward soul, funk, and blues — with artists like 'Fast' Eddie Smith and the 'Sticks' McGhee/John Lee Hooker pairing featured prominently — though the full depth of the catalog is unknown.

Despite being described as 'very highly rated,' the shop has a notably thin third-party review footprint. No Discogs seller ratings, Yelp reviews, Google reviews, or Facebook reviews were available in the sourced data — which is a meaningful gap for a record shop, where platforms like Discogs transaction history typically serve as the gold standard for trust and reliability. The loc8nearme.com listing returned only broken web template code, offering no substantive data. This lack of verifiable external ratings makes it difficult to fully corroborate the 'highly rated' characterization, and prospective buyers should seek out the shop's Discogs profile (if one exists) before making significant purchases.

Overall, 939 Records appears to be a legitimate, professionally operated online record shop with a clear regional identity and a functional e-commerce presence. It is best suited for Pittsburgh-area collectors and remote buyers interested in soul, funk, and blues vinyl who prefer a curated online shopping experience. However, the shop would benefit greatly from building a more visible review presence on established platforms like Discogs, Yelp, or Google to substantiate its claimed reputation and attract new customers with confidence.
